competitors.title: How Async AI Agent Workflows Survive Failures
key_points: Durable long-running execution with persistent state checkpointing decouples task submission from completion
Four recurring problems: infrastructure timeouts, process crashes, human approval blocks, active state growth
API Gateway 29s, Azure Functions 230s, Lambda 900s timeout ceilings — raising thresholds turns clean errors into silent ones

State checkpointing captures agent execution to durable storage before each step; chat-only recovery achieves only 8-13% correctness vs 100% for semantics-aware checkpoint/restore (Crab paper, Terminal-Bench)
Three state categories: working memory, active execution state, long-term memory
Per-step snapshot (LangGraph) vs event history replay (Temporal) comparison with storage cost, exactly-once, and history limit tradeoffs
Graceful degradation ladder: retry with backoff → Retry-After → circuit breaker + failover → cached response → simplified reasoning → HITL → dead letter queue
Checkpoint-interrupt-resume pattern for human-in-the-loop approvals
Short-term memory with summarization vs long-term cross-session semantic memory (MemGPT virtual memory model)

competitors.title: Beyond Try/Except: Implementing the Saga Pattern in 2026 AI Agents
key_points: Enterprise agentics in May 2026 has moved past simple chat loops to multi-step business operations
Saga Pattern: for every forward-facing action node, map a backward-facing compensating node
LangGraph v1.2 introduces built-in node-level error handlers and state-routing commands
Compensation chain executes in reverse order to clean up workspace on unrecoverable exceptions
Three benefits: data integrity across external systems, resilience against brittle infinite-retry loops, deterministic fallbacks with clean diagnostic logs
Key insight: 'The hallmark of a senior AI Architect in 2026 is designing the graph that fails gracefully'

competitors.title: AI Agent Workflow Orchestration on GPU Cloud: Temporal, Inngest, and Restate (2026)
key_points: Naive agent loops break in production due to timeout cascades, partial tool calls with duplicate side effects, and retry storms on GPU ($5-15/hr per card)
Three durable execution models: history-based replay (Temporal), step journaling (Inngest), virtual objects/journal (Restate)
Temporal: strongest for long multi-day workflows, configurable heartbeats, highest production maturity
Inngest: best for event-driven serverless pipelines, step-level retries, concurrency caps
Restate: native exactly-once semantics via virtual objects, no idempotency keys needed, best for stateful per-session agents
Cost analysis: crash without durable execution wastes $17.75 per 3.5hr H100 failure; with checkpointing, $1.27 per crash
Production checklist: idempotency keys, heartbeat interval <50% of timeout, compensation logic, structured logs, workflow backlog alerts, replay correctness testing

competitors.title: Build AI Agents That Resume from Failure with Pydantic AI + Prefect
key_points: PrefectAgent wrapper adds production capabilities: retry policies, durable execution, observability without changing agent logic
Separate retry configs for model calls (3 retries, exponential backoff) vs tool invocations (2 retries, faster backoff)
Durable execution: Prefect caches successful task results; on retry, skips completed steps and resumes from failure point
Custom cache policy ignores timestamps/run_ids to avoid unique cache keys on retries
Three composition patterns: agent output feeds downstream tasks, multiple agents in sequence, conditional workflows
Cost savings: single GPT-5 call ~$0.006; 10 LLM calls failing at end wastes $0.06 per retry without caching

competitors.title: Build Reliable AI Agents with Durable Execution | Pydantic AI + DBOS
key_points: DBOS is a lightweight durable execution library built directly on Postgres — no external workflow engine needed
DBOSAgent wrapper auto-converts agent.run() into durable workflow; model calls and MCP communication checkpointed as steps
Sub-agent calls automatically become child workflows with independent checkpointing and observability
Fan-out/fan-in pattern for parallel search workflows with DBOS.start_workflow_async
Integration with Logfire for end-to-end OpenTelemetry traces across agent runs, model requests, and tool invocations
DBOS Conductor web UI for visualizing, canceling, restarting, or forking workflows

competitors.title: Applying Site Reliability Engineering to Autonomous AI Agents (Microsoft, May 2026)
key_points: Agents fail in ways SRE tooling cannot see: HTTP 200, normal latency, zero errors, but agent approved unauthorized transaction or burned $800 in reasoning loop
Safety SLI: measures whether agent acted within policy (not just whether it responded correctly)
Error budget drives agent autonomy decisions: clean safety record earns autonomy, budget exhaustion triggers CIRCUIT_BREAK
Circuit breakers for agent-specific failure modes: policy bypass, LLM provider error, tool timeout, trust score degradation, reasoning loop/deadlock
Reasoning loop detection: max_iterations=15, max_tokens_per_session=50000, repetition_threshold=0.85
Chaos engineering for agents: fault injection for LLM degradation, trust manipulation, tool timeout cascades
Replay debugging: record every agent session as replayable artifact for exact incident reproduction

competitors.title: Handling Failures in Agent-Based Workflows (April 2026)
key_points: Four failure types: tool failures (API timeout, invalid response), reasoning failures (hallucination, wrong tool selection), state failures (lost context), execution failures (code errors)
Six strategies: retry with exponential backoff, fallback strategy, validation layer, circuit breaker pattern, human-in-the-loop, logging and observability
Validation layer acts as quality gate to filter hallucinations and prevent garbage outputs from propagating
Circuit breaker prevents repeated failures and protects system resources with cooldown recovery

LangGraph v1.2 (2026) introduces built-in node-level error handlers with Saga pattern support via error_handler parameter
Temporal history limit: 51,200 events / 50MB per workflow; workflows exceeding it use Continue-As-New
